title: Multiplayer Erosion Simulation on Heightmap Terrain
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements a multiplayer erosion simulation on a heightmap terrain. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Create a 128x128 grid heightmap terrain using PlaneGeometry with 127 width/height segments. Initial heights should be generated using layered simplex/perlin-style noise (use sine-based approximation: combine 4 octaves of sin/cos at different frequencies and amplitudes). The terrain mesh should use MeshStandardMaterial with vertex coloring based on height (blue < 0.1, green 0.1-0.5, brown 0.5-0.8, white > 0.8). Heights should be normalized to range [0, 1].
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 80, 100) looking at origin. OrbitControls enabled.
- Lighting: DirectionalLight from (50, 100, 50) intensity 1.0, AmbientLight intensity 0.3.
- Add a subtle wireframe overlay toggle for the terrain.

## Player System (Simulated Multiplayer)
- Support 2 players: Player 1 (Red cursor, WASD keys) and Player 2 (Blue cursor, Arrow keys).
- Each player has a visible sphere cursor on the terrain surface (radius 2 units) showing their erosion brush position.
- Player cursors start at grid positions: P1 at (32, 32), P2 at (96, 96).
- Players move their cursors across the terrain grid. Cursors snap to terrain height.
- Each player has an independent erosion brush radius (default 5 cells) and erosion strength (default 0.02).

## Erosion Simulation
- When a player presses their action key (P1: Space, P2: Enter), hydraulic erosion is applied at their cursor position.
- Erosion algorithm: For each cell within brush radius, reduce height by strength * (1 - distance/radius). Displaced sediment is distributed to the lowest neighboring cell (thermal erosion component). Total volume must be conserved: sum of all height changes across the entire grid must equal zero (sediment is moved, not destroyed).
- Implement a global rain erosion mode toggled by pressing 'R'. When active, random droplets (10 per frame) fall on the terrain, each removing a tiny amount (0.001) from impact point and depositing it at the lowest neighbor. Track total rain erosion cycles.
- Implement an UNDO system: pressing 'Z' undoes the last manual erosion action (up to 10 steps). Pressing 'Y' redoes. Undo/redo stack is shared across both players.

## Conservation & Physics
- Track totalVolume: sum of all heights across the entire 128x128 grid. This value must remain constant (within epsilon 0.001) after any erosion operation.
- Track minHeight and maxHeight across the terrain at all times.
- No height value may ever be NaN or negative.
- Sediment that flows off the grid edge is redistributed to the nearest edge cell (no volume loss).

## HUD / DOM UI
- Top-left panel showing: Player 1 position (grid x,y), Player 2 position (grid x,y), Total Volume, Min Height, Max Height, Undo stack size, Redo stack size, Rain mode status (ON/OFF), Erosion cycle count.
- A button with id='btn-reset' that resets terrain to initial state.
- A button with id='btn-wireframe' that toggles wireframe overlay.
- A slider with id='slider-p1-radius' (range 1-15, default 5) controlling Player 1 brush radius.
- A slider with id='slider-p2-strength' (range 0.005-0.05, step 0.005, default 0.02) controlling Player 2 erosion strength.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- terrain: { width: 128, height: 128, totalVolume: number, minHeight: number, maxHeight: number, initialTotalVolume: number, heightAt: function(x,y) returning height at grid position }
- player1: { gridX: number, gridY: number, worldX: number, worldY: number, worldZ: number, brushRadius: number, erosionStrength: number, erosionCount: number }
- player2: { gridX: number, gridY: number, worldX: number, worldY: number, worldZ: number, brushRadius: number, erosionStrength: number, erosionCount: number }
- undoStack: { size: number, maxSize: 10 }
- redoStack: { size: number }
- rainMode: { active: boolean, cycleCount: number }
- wireframeVisible: boolean
- frameCount: number
- conservationError: number (absolute difference between current totalVolume and initialTotalVolume)
physics_constraints: Volume conservation: the sum of all terrain heights must remain constant (within epsilon 0.001) after any erosion operation. No height may be NaN or negative. Sediment displaced by erosion must be deposited at valid neighboring cells. Edge sediment must not be lost — redistribute to nearest edge cell. Thermal erosion flows downhill only. Undo must perfectly restore previous heightmap state.
